title: Ukraine Strikes St. Petersburg — Kronstadt Naval Base (Corvette Boikiy Set Ablaze), Oil Terminal, Tambov Defense Facility; 350+ Drones; Day 1,560
detail: On June 3, 2026 (Day 1,560), Ukraine launched one of its deepest and most strategically significant long-range drone attacks of the war, striking targets in and around St. Petersburg — approximately 1,200–1,400 km from Ukrainian territory. The attack commenced hours before the opening of Putin's St. Petersburg International Economic Forum (SPIEF), often called 'Putin's Davos.' Key targets struck: (1) Kronstadt naval base — a Russian guided-missile corvette, the Boikiy, was set on fire while in dry dock, marking Ukraine's farthest naval strike of the war; (2) St. Petersburg's largest oil transshipment terminal in the northern port district was struck, causing fires; (3) a defense-related facility in Tambov Oblast was also struck. Three districts of St. Petersburg were affected by drone impacts and/or debris. Russia's defense ministry claimed to have intercepted 350+ Ukrainian drones across the night's operations. Several people were wounded in St. Petersburg. Ukraine's SBU (Security Service) confirmed the operation, describing it as targeting Russia's military-industrial capacity and energy export infrastructure. President Zelensky stated the strikes were a 'justified and necessary response' to Russia's ongoing mass aerial bombardment of Ukrainian cities. The SPIEF attack timing carried clear symbolic weight — Russia was hosting global business leaders at the moment its second city was under drone attack.

title: Russian Strikes Kill 3, Hit 17 Settlements in Kharkiv Region — Day 1,560
detail: On June 3, 2026 (Day 1,560), Russian forces attacked Kharkiv city and 17 other settlements across Kharkiv Oblast with drone strikes. A Russian drone struck a multi-story residential building in Kharkiv, causing a fire. Three civilians were killed across the region, and 19 people were wounded in residential areas over the two-day period June 2–3. The Kharkiv region has faced sustained Russian strikes throughout the war given its proximity to the Russian border (~40 km from Kharkiv city to the Russian frontier). Russia's cross-border drone and rocket attacks on Kharkiv Oblast continued unabated through late May and early June 2026 as Russia maintained pressure on Ukraine's second-largest city. The front line in Kharkiv Oblast has remained relatively stable since Russia's failed attempt to capture Kharkiv in spring 2024, but cross-border fire has been constant.

title: 5 Killed, 11 Wounded in Donetsk Region; 279 Front-Line Combat Engagements on Day 1,560
detail: On June 3, 2026 (Day 1,560), Russian forces killed 5 civilians and wounded 11 more in the Donetsk region of Ukraine in the 24-hour period. Ukraine's General Staff recorded 279 combat engagements across the entire front line — continuing the pattern of high-intensity combat that characterized late May 2026. The Pokrovsk sector remained one of the most active, with Russian forces repeatedly attempting to advance west after capturing Pokrovsk city in early 2026. Ukraine's 28th Mechanized Brigade established drone control over Russian-occupied Horlivka (Donetsk Oblast), demonstrating Ukraine's expanding drone warfare capacity. Ukraine also struck Russian UAV crews, air defense units, and warehouses at the former Donetsk Airport, now used by Russia as a military logistics hub. Despite 279 engagements, Russia's advance rates in Donetsk Oblast remained low — ISW noted Russia's spring-summer 2026 offensive had largely stalled at a rate of approximately 2.9 sq km/day.
